claims.text: SPS at 1900 °C and 40 MPa for 10 min will produce single-phase ZrB2 with greater than 98% theoretical density.
The SPS treatment will reduce residual porosity to below 2 vol%.
SPS will densify ZrB2 at approximately 400 °C below the temperature required for conventional pressureless sintering.
The higher density and lower residual porosity produced by SPS will minimize internal holes and preserve structural integrity during prolonged liquid-plating-bath exposure.
The starting ZrB2 powder has a particle size of 1–5 µm.
The starting ZrB2 powder bears native ZrO2 and B2O3 surface layers.
The cold-pressed green body has approximately 40% porosity.
Localized plasma during SPS enhances neck formation between ZrB2 particles.
Localized plasma removes native surface oxides from ZrB2 particles.
Enhanced neck formation and oxide removal promote rapid mass transport, pore closure, and disruption of connected residual porosity.
Pulsed DC current produces Joule heating at ZrB2 particle contacts.
SPS generates transient plasma that cleans oxide-covered ZrB2 particle surfaces.
Contact heating and plasma-assisted cleaning accelerate diffusion and permit densification at a lower bulk temperature.
After 100 h in a 900 °C plating bath, SPS-processed ZrB2 will retain at least 90% of its as-sintered flexural strength.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will exhibit minimal new pore formation during 100 h of exposure to a 900 °C plating bath.
Conventional pressureless sintering at 2300 °C yields ZrB2 with approximately 92% theoretical density.
Conventionally pressureless-sintered ZrB2 contains approximately 5 vol% residual porosity.
Conventionally pressureless-sintered ZrB2 has an initial flexural strength of approximately 500 MPa.
After 100 h in the plating bath, conventionally sintered ZrB2 loses more than 50% of its strength and falls below 250 MPa.
Long-term molten-bath exposure effects on SPS-processed ZrB2 remain untested.
